prompt: In a completely dominant, single-locus model, which cross predicts a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive phenotype ratio?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: The four equally likely outcomes are AA, Aa, Aa and aa. A sample ratio is evidence, not an exact guarantee.

prompt: A double heterozygote carries linked alleles in the phase GT/gt. What can produce Gt and gT gametes?
answer: Crossing over between the two loci
options: Crossing over between the two loci
Independent segregation of alleles on an unchanged same chromosome
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: A crossover between loci can exchange chromosome segments and form nonparental allele combinations.

cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: A recessive tester helps distinguish the possible genotypes behind a dominant phenotype; sample size affects certainty when no recessive offspring appear.

prompt: Assume independent assortment and complete dominance at both loci. What phenotype ratio is predicted for TtYy × TtYy?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Each locus predicts a 3:1 phenotype ratio. Multiplying independent probabilities gives 9/16, 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16.

prompt: Tallness T is completely dominant to t. Flower alleles R1/R2 show incomplete dominance, with heterozygotes pink. What offspring result from TTR1R1 × ttR2R2?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Each parent supplies only one gamete type; heterozygosity has different phenotype rules at the two loci.

prompt: A heterozygote is tall for one trait but intermediate pink for another. Which inheritance description fits the stated model?
answer: Complete dominance for height and incomplete dominance for colour
options: Complete dominance for height and incomplete dominance for colour
Codominance for height and Y linkage for colour
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Dominance relationships must be evaluated separately at each locus.

prompt: In a hypothetical single-locus trait, B is dominant to b. An individual with the dominant phenotype has a recessive-phenotype child with a bb partner. What is the first parent’s genotype?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: The recessive child is bb and must receive b from both parents; the dominant-phenotype parent must also carry B.

prompt: Under a fully penetrant autosomal-recessive model, two unaffected carriers have a child. What is the probability the child is affected?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Aa × Aa predicts aa in one of four equally likely genotype combinations. Earlier births do not change this probability.

prompt: In an explicitly additive model with equally contributing loci and no environmental variation, AABBCC is crossed with aabbcc. What is predicted?
answer: All AaBbCc offspring with an intermediate model value
options: All AaBbCc offspring with an intermediate model value
Every offspring has either extreme parental genotype
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: All F1 offspring receive the same intermediate number of contributing alleles in this simplified additive model.

prompt: In a fully penetrant autosomal-dominant model, two affected parents have an unaffected child. What must both parents be?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: An unaffected child is aa; both affected parents must be able to supply a, making each Aa.

prompt: A model has red homozygotes, white homozygotes and pink heterozygotes. What inheritance relationship is shown?
options: Codominance with separate red and white patches
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: The heterozygous phenotype is intermediate under the specified model.

prompt: In persons with sickle-cell disease, the red blood cells are shaped like a “sickle” and are not biconcave disks like normal red blood cells. Mr. and Mrs. Charleson are both carriers ( Hb A Hb S ) of sickle-cell disease. What are the chances of their having a child with sickle-cell disease?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: For HbA/HbS × HbA/HbS, the HbS/HbS combination has probability 1/4 in each conception under the stated model.

prompt: Two independent completely dominant loci have parental genotypes AABB × aabb. What describes the F1?
answer: All AaBb with both dominant phenotypes
options: All AaBb with both dominant phenotypes
Four phenotype classes in a 1:1:1:1 ratio
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Only AB and ab parental gametes are available, producing identical heterozygous combinations at these loci.

prompt: For independent AaBb × AaBb, what is the probability of the dominant A phenotype together with bb?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: P(A_) = 3/4 and P(bb) = 1/4; their product is 3/16.

prompt: In a fully penetrant recessive model, an aa mother has an affected daughter and an unaffected son. What must their father’s genotype be?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: The father supplies a to the affected child and A to the unaffected child, so he carries both alleles.

prompt: A heterozygous affected parent Aa and an unaffected parent aa have offspring in a fully penetrant dominant model. What affected probability is predicted?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Aa × aa gives one-half Aa and one-half aa. The statement is conditional on the inheritance model.

prompt: The feather colour in some species of chickens is governed by two dominant alleles (co-dominance). Black birds are homozygous for the B allele and white birds are homozygous for the W allele. Predict the phenotype of the F 1 generation when a black rooster is crossed with a white hen?
answer: 100 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage.
options: 100 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black plumage and 50 percent of the chicks will have white plumage.
100 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage, and 50 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: BB × WW gives all BW offspring; with codominance both products are expressed rather than an intermediate grey phenotype.

prompt: In fruit flies the gene for eye colour is found on the X chromosome. In these flies, red eye colour is dominant to white-eye colour. Predict the probability of producing white-eyed male offspring in a cross between a female fly that is homozygous for red eye colour and a male fly that has white eyes.
answer: 0 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
options: 100 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
75 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
25 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
0 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Every son receives a dominant red-eye X from the homozygous mother and a Y from the father, so none is white-eyed in this model.

prompt: Assume independent assortment and complete dominance. What phenotype ratio is predicted for RrPp × rrpp?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: The double heterozygote forms RP, Rp, rP and rp gametes equally; the tester forms rp only.

prompt: In the standard ABO model, what is the probability of type A from IAi × IAi?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: IAIA and IAi produce type A; ii produces O. Three of four combinations are type A.

prompt: A test cross yields 420 parental and 80 recombinant offspring. What is the approximate short-interval map distance?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Recombination frequency is 80/(420 + 80) × 100 = 16%, corresponding to about 16 cM in the stated approximation.

prompt: A carrier mother XAXa and unaffected father XAY have a son. Under a fully penetrant X-linked recessive model, what is the probability that this son is affected?
cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
explanation: Conditioning on a son leaves XAY and XaY equally likely. The all-children affected probability would instead be 1/4.
